note: TAIpei RUSH (東京狂飆, https://www.taipei-rush.app/tokyo/) is capture-class: a Vite/rolldown production build of an open-world Tokyo driving/racing game (kart races, story missions, live transit/stock feeds), served under the /tokyo/ sub-path by Vercel; the same origin also serves the Taipei-rooted deploy at "/" whose shared files (avatars, root icons/title art, base-stripped assets/… forms) are part of this capture because the Tokyo bundle carries matching literals. §0.4 fork-over-mirror was checked on 2026-10-13 — the page and its JS reference no public source repo (see README), so the mirror stands. Derived pipeline: capture → pinned prettier 3.9.6 (module API, default options, formatted to a layout fixed point, 1-2 passes — never the CLI: it respects .gitignore and can silently echo its input) → readable/<served path>.pretty.js|css per captured JS/CSS file (the capture preserves the served URL structure, so the derived layers MIRROR it — nested directories, no __-flattening; every pretty provably NOT byte-identical to its capture source) → statement-aligned slices src/<served path>-NN.js of every APP chunk (top-level declaration boundaries only, ~250-350 line windows; oversized single declarations stay whole) with an exact 2-line provenance header. The identifier rename campaign (PLAN §5) is applied to the app slices: top-level bindings and import aliases of a chunk get semantic names (tools/names.json), written by tools/apply-names.mjs with a scope-aware token pass, recovered mechanically into rename-map.json (tools/recover-scoped-map.mjs: token alignment, non-identifier positions identical) and re-applied by tools/derive.mjs through that recorded map — `files` word-boundary records plus `scoped` token-index records. Public API names (the export tables) and vendor identifiers keep their served names; names that appear as object-literal/destructuring shorthands or as unaliased exports are excluded (documented in README). Every slice parses standalone under `node --input-type=module --check -` and round-trips byte-exact to its recorded readable line range (through the recorded rename map where the chunk is renamed). Vendor rule — wholeFile sections, never sliced: tokyo/assets/three-C4coU-vx.js (bundled three.js r186 engine: WebGLRenderer + __THREE__ r186 revision registration), avatars/basis/basis_transcoder.js (Google Basis KTX2 transcoder wrapper) and _vercel/insights/script.js (Vercel Web Analytics platform script) — all content-anchored and guarded. Stylesheet rule — every captured .css is wholeFile. Non-standalone parts are skipped sections, indexed but never sliced: every app chunk's final export {…} table (the bindings live in the earlier slices; its public names are the capture's public API and are never renamed). Inline <script>/<style> scan: tokyo/index.html carries 9 inline <script> blocks (the cross-deploy region-redirect shims, the ?region= alias, the language gate, the loader overlay + boot watchdog + key-art driver, and the error/save shims) and 2 inline <style> blocks (the loader CSS and the loader-overlay CSS) — each gets a wholeFile twin plus a readable/index-inline-map.json entry with its exact byte range and sha256. Binary payloads (webp key art, glb avatars, woff2 font, .bin animation bank, png/svg icons) are hashed notRendered records (bytes + sha256), never prettified. The bundle also carries its own QA race harness (?kart=<circuit>&kartmode=race, tokyo/assets/region-tokyo-*.js) — used only for the boot evidence, never modifying the capture. Capture bytes are untouched by everything above; re-cut with `node tools/derive.mjs` after any capture refresh. `node tools/audit.js` is the gate.
